genieCoverage: Only Genie Spaces usage carries a space ID. This table does not cover all Genie costs; budgets are not available from system tables.
pricingModeNote: The deployment setting controls which price tables are read. List-price baselines remain visible; changing this setting requires a pipeline refresh and app redeployment.
contractCoverage: Contract rates cover {{percent}}% of observed list-price spend in this scope.
consultative: Read-only analysis. You approve and apply every change.
overviewDescription: Understand your spend. Prioritize the changes worth investigating.
trackedNote: Valued from observed configuration changes; not an invoice reconciliation.
emptyHint: Try another workspace or check source permissions in Data health.
errorHint: Check your workspace connection and permissions, then try again.
notFound: This resource was not found in your accessible scope.
dailySpendNote: USD · selected window · list prices unless noted
topActionsNote: Ranked by estimated savings, effort and priority. Overlapping actions are not added twice.
resourceDescription: Compare alternatives, inspect evidence and validate the proposed change.
noLink: Workspace URL unavailable; use the resource ID in Databricks.
chartUnavailable: No compatible time series is available. Inspect the measurements below.

rulesNote: Rules provide evidence and scenarios. Nothing changes your resources automatically.

executionNote: Data queries run as the app service principal. Your authenticated identity defines the workspace scope.
contractNote: Blended: contract rates where covered, list prices otherwise. Not an invoice total.
appNote: Lifecycle events do not measure request traffic. This inventory does not infer app idleness or savings.
genieNote: Genie usage and costs are analysis only, not cost-saving recommendations.

name: Name
noUsage: No observed usage in the selected window

resetHint: Clear filters to return to all accessible opportunities.

prose.untrackedEndpoint: No request has ever been logged for this endpoint, in this window or in the ~90 days of request history system tables keep. That is what an unused endpoint looks like, but also what you see when usage tracking is off for it: system.serving.endpoint_usage only records endpoints with usage tracking enabled. Check the endpoint's Metrics tab (or ask its owner) before acting.
prose.unpricedPool: We can't tell what this pool costs. Its warm instances are cloud VMs billed by your cloud provider and never appear in Databricks billing, so no saving is shown. Check this node type's hourly price on your cloud bill, times the warm instances kept around the clock.
prose.unwrittenSources: {{count}} of the job's {{total}} source tables ({{tables}}) show no write at all in the window. If they are static reference data, the finding stands. If something outside Databricks writes them (a Delta Sharing provider, a federated or external table, another engine), lineage can't see those writes and these runs may have had new input. Check the tables' history before changing the trigger.
prose.rangeDbuOnly: Low = the DBU-only saving billing can prove; high = adds the estimated cloud-VM cost Databricks doesn't expose per warehouse for classic/pro. The gap is that estimate's uncertainty.
prose.rangeSharedCluster: Low = $0: this cluster is also used interactively, so moving the jobs to job compute may not let it shrink; high = the full measured all-purpose vs jobs price gap if it does.
prose.rangeNoJobsRate: Low = $0: the jobs-compute rate wasn't in list_prices for this cloud, so the figure is a conservative {{pct}}% of the reassignable spend, not a measured price gap.
prose.rangeAutostopTiers: Low = the reclaim from simply turning auto-stop on at a safe {{baseline}}-minute setting (almost no restart cost); high = the full {{proposed}}-minute setting, including the tightening that adds ~{{stops}} restarts/day.
prose.rangeAutostopConservative: Low = the reclaim from a conservative, low-churn auto-stop setting; high = the full {{proposed}}-minute setting, which adds ~{{stops}} extra restarts/day.
prose.rangeAutostopChurn: Low = $0 if the ~{{stops}} extra restarts/day a {{proposed}}-min auto-stop adds aren't acceptable for this warehouse's users; high = the full idle-tail reclaim if they are.
prose.rangeRightsizeInferred: Low = $0: without Spark task data the target size is inferred from query behaviour, so treat it as directional; high = the full one-step rate cut if {{size}} keeps up with the workload.
prose.rangeRightsizeFloor: Low = the one measured step to {{size}} (peak slot demand fits with room to spare); high = {{floor}}, the deeper size the measured headroom could reach, one step at a time.
prose.rangeRightsizeDeeper: Low = the one measured step to {{size}} (peak slot demand fits with room to spare); high = the deeper size the measured headroom could reach, one step at a time.
